answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Hairspring maker mainspring assay stamped by the master warrant changes that arithmetic: each mainspring is a measured rate sheet plus a master signature, so a farm must coil a hundred real hairsprings by hand, so the inlet for each fake is paid in the real world. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the willow of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The garden is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
